title: Visitor and Portrait
premise: Wendell Quintana's late-night call-in show becomes a séance when the voices on the line belong to listeners who died days earlier, each asking her to 'sign for them.' Her sleep recordings reveal a second voice — a woman named Ada Voss, who died in 1974 and has been answering Wendell's questions in her sleep, trading answers for a place in a living body. The dead are counting down to a signing ceremony at the abandoned Voss family house, where the last living resident will transfer ownership of every soul in the ledger. Wendell discovers she is that last resident through an adoption she never knew about; getting the surviving Voss relatives out of town before the final count is the only way to void the papers. In the end she burns the ledger with herself still named inside it, choosing erasure over belonging, and wakes to a show with no callers at all.
about_author: Xanthe Amberdale is the pen name of a former overnight radio producer who spent years logging dead air and insists the quietest hours hold the most voices. She writes horror from a farmhouse whose previous owners politely declined to be researched.

chapters.title: Dead Air, Live Callers
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. During a storm-blackened broadcast, callers phone in with intimate details of their own deaths — details confirmed by morning obituaries. Wendell, compulsive documenter, begins transcribing every call, treating the log as prayer. The emotional beat is dread braided with professional denial: she keeps hosting because stopping would mean admitting the show is real.

chapters.title: The Second Voice
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV, interleaved with transcripts. Reviewing her sleep recordings, she hears herself ask questions and a stranger — Ada Voss, dead since 1974 — answer: names, dates, the location of the old Voss house. Ada offers knowledge in exchange for 'a warm room.' The beat shifts from dread to complicity as Wendell realizes she's already been negotiating in her sleep.

chapters.title: The Count
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Ada. At the derelict Voss house, Wendell finds a ledger of residents, living and dead, and learns she's the last living signatory via a sealed adoption record. The dead gather nightly for a headcount; each night the count grows closer to quorum. Ada, desperate for embodiment, both helps and betrays her. The beat is vertigo: home revealed as trap.

chapters.title: Signature
chapters.summary: Climax and resolution, Wendell's POV. On the final night she evacuates the scattered Voss descendants before dawn, voiding quorum, then faces Ada alone in the parlor. Offered belonging — a family, a name, survival — Wendell burns the ledger with her own name inside. The count collapses; the lines go silent. Final beat: grief disguised as peace, a host with no one calling.
